name: Minny Pops
label: Factory Records
lede: A very tall Amsterdammer named his band after a Korg drum box, planned three gigs and an EP, and instead got signed in a Joy Division dressing room and became the first Dutch band to record a Peel session.

eras.title: Three gigs and an EP, supposedly
eras.text: Wally van Middendorp came out of Amsterdam's Ultra scene, a city of squats and art-punk, with a label of his own and a rhythm box. Minny Pops were meant to be a short conceptual run: electronic, minimal, repetitive. Then Rough Trade started distributing the album.

years.src: LTM: Minny Pops · Electronic Sound
years.h: Van Middendorp's first record: 'We're So Glad Elvis Is Dead'
years.p: [[Wally van Middendorp|127099e8-d01e-42d4-8ee9-0b31905ce8f3]] starts the Plurex label and debuts as Tits, with 'We're So Glad Elvis Is Dead' and 'Daddy Is My Pusher'.

years.src: LTM: Minny Pops · Electronic Sound · Wikipedia: Minny Pops
years.h: A Korg Mini Pops rhythm box gives the band its name
years.p: Van Middendorp on vocals and drum machine, Frans Hagenaars on bass, Peter Mertens on guitar, plus two dancers, one of them Wally's brother Rob.
years.xp:
"The idea was that it would be a conceptual thing, three gigs and an EP and that would be it," van Middendorp told Electronic Sound. "We had an idea to play something that was electronic and minimalist, and to use repetition to push boundaries."

He remembered the Amsterdam of the time as tense: "there was a squatters' building, and the army came in with tanks to evict them."

years.src: LTM: Minny Pops
years.h: First show at the Brakke Grond, with dancers
years.p: Minny Pops debut at the Brakke Grond in Amsterdam: distorted guitar and bass over a drum machine, which plenty in the room didn't know what to do with.
years.xp: "A lot of people couldn't understand the visuals or the sounds because we were working with distorted guitars and bass," van Middendorp said.

years.src: LTM: Minny Pops · Wikipedia: Minny Pops
years.h: Kojak, Plurex 005
years.p: The first Minny Pops record: 'Kojak' with 'Footsteps' and 'Nervous'.

years.src: LTM: Minny Pops · Wikipedia: Minny Pops
years.h: Sounds: "the liveliest and strangest album I've heard all year"
years.p: Rough Trade distribution carries Drastic Measures, Drastic Movement (Plurex 900) into Britain, where Sounds' Dave McCullough goes for it.
years.xp: McCullough also called it "a fine album filled with contemporary, electronic consciousness." By June 1979 guitarists Dennis Duchhart and Stef Emmer had come in. Support slots that year included Red Crayola and Scritti Politti at the Melkweg and XTC at the Paradiso.

eras.title: Gretton's Dutch discovery
eras.text: Two support slots with Joy Division turned an Amsterdam art band into a Factory act. Within a year Minny Pops had a Martin Hannett single, a Peel session, an East Coast tour and a reputation for standing very still.

years.src: Electronic Sound · LTM: Minny Pops · The Quietus
years.h: Rob Gretton offers a Factory deal in the Eindhoven dressing room
years.p: Minny Pops support [[Joy Division|9a58fda3-f4ed-4080-a3a5-f457aac9fcdd]] in Den Haag and Eindhoven. After the Eindhoven show, Joy Division's manager [[Rob Gretton|41b55fab-da3b-4ecf-a67d-aeeec338a9c5]] comes backstage with an offer.
years.xp: Electronic Sound reports that a local motorcycle gang crashed the Eindhoven venue about 20 minutes into Joy Division's set.

years.src: Electronic Sound · LTM: Minny Pops
years.h: Forty minutes of provocation before the Bury riot
years.p: Minny Pops open Joy Division's show at Derby Hall, Bury, needling the crowd for 40 minutes. [[Ian Curtis|10ae1bf6-88b2-4fb4-8fbe-8227a49803d3]] is too unwell to sing the whole set and the night turns into a riot.
years.xp: Crispy Ambulance's Alan Hempsall sang a couple of songs in Curtis's place and [[Section 25|82e26f64-813d-4b22-a442-44d182f7f9eb]] joined on stage. Three days later, on April 11, Minny Pops played the Factory at Manchester's Russell Club on Gretton's invitation.

years.cap: Minny Pops' bassist at Hal 4, Rotterdam, December 13, 1980
q: Did we confuse audiences? Oh, very much.
years.src: LTM: Minny Pops · Electronic Sound
years.h: Arms folded, standing still for a minute after every song
years.p: NME's Andy Gill saw them supporting Joy Division and noticed the habit. Another NME writer described van Middendorp as a wiry giant who barely moved.
years.xp:
Van Middendorp explained the standstills to Electronic Sound: "it wasn't about the applause, it was about allowing the musicians on stage to reflect on their performance."

Electronic Sound puts him at six foot six. NME's Mick Duffy went further: "approaching seven feet tall... a caricatured Elvis Costello on stilts."

years.src: LTM: Minny Pops · Wikipedia: Minny Pops
years.h: Wim Dekker's synthesizer becomes the band's core
years.p: [[Wim Dekker|21604248-b51e-41af-9e76-d59cc629e2f4]] joins on synth and becomes van Middendorp's musical partner. Leon van Zoeren takes bass and Gerard Walhof guitar.

years.src: Keeping It Peel · LTM: Minny Pops
years.h: The first Dutch band to record a Peel session
years.p: BBC Radio 1 broadcasts their [[John Peel|e4dec348-ad10-43b6-a2b1-c22aab890675]] session: 'Dolphin's Spurt', 'Mono', 'Jets' and 'Ice Cube Wall'. The same month they play the LSE with [[A Certain Ratio|73577e86-4da8-4d76-949d-34c757e053be]] and the [[Au Pairs|d350bc0e-10bb-47f1-9027-d1f011ae9aa8]].

years.src: LTM: Minny Pops · Electronic Sound · Wikipedia: Minny Pops
yt: 'Lights', live at Hurrah, New York, January 1981
years.h: Seven dates on the US East Coast, about $700 down
years.p: After supporting [[New Order|f1106b17-dcbb-45f6-b938-199ccfab50cc]] in Rotterdam, Minny Pops tour New York, Hoboken, Toronto and Boston, rare for a mainland European band then.
years.xp: Electronic Sound dates their Peppermint Lounge show in New York to January 10, 1981, with Suicide's [[Alan Vega|dd720ac8-1c68-4484-abb7-0546413a55e3]] in the room. The Toronto Globe and Mail decided the result was "not unlistenable or uninteresting."

years.src: LTM: Minny Pops · The Quietus · Electronic Sound · Wikipedia: Minny Pops
years.h: Martin Hannett produces Fac 31, sometimes from the floor
years.p: Recorded at Strawberry Studios, Stockport, with 'Goddess' on the B-side. 'Dolphin's Spurt' reaches No. 23 on the UK indie chart.
years.xp:
"Sometimes he laid down on the floor of the mixing room for half an hour at least, just thinking," van Middendorp said of [[Martin Hannett|ffbfce58-5185-4bcc-8c45-a7cd5d1a3783]]. Years later he told The Quietus, "He was there somewhere, I guess"; engineer Chris Nagle did much of the mix. The keyboard player nearly cried when he couldn't hear himself on it.

Alan Erasmus wrote to say the single needed a repress. Van Middendorp remembered the message: "It's not about the money, it's about the fun of releasing the record."

years.src: The Quietus
years.h: Rob Gretton welcomes his house guest
years.p: Staying with [[Rob Gretton|41b55fab-da3b-4ecf-a67d-aeeec338a9c5]], van Middendorp sat in his host's chair with the TV remote. Gretton ordered the "Dutch fuck face" out of it.
years.xp: Van Middendorp told The Quietus he came to understand it as Northern humour, taking the piss to make a guest feel at home.

years.src: LTM: Minny Pops · Wikipedia: Minny Pops
years.h: Gerard Walhof leaves, and Minny Pops play their last show
years.p: Walhof isn't replaced, which delays the second album. Bassist Pieter Mulder and drummer Orpheus Roovers are in the line-up that plays the final live dates in December.

eras.title: Disco and doom, then Streetlife
eras.text: The second album came out on Factory Benelux after the band had already stopped playing live. Van Middendorp and Dekker kept writing, for the theatre and for the dancefloor, until a meeting in 1983 ended Minny Pops.

years.src: LTM: Minny Pops
years.h: Van Middendorp hosts Crépuscule's 'Dialogue North-South' tour
years.p: He's master of ceremonies for the Les Disques du Crépuscule package tour of France and the Low Countries. His patter turns up as 'Raving Lunatic' on a Crépuscule compilation.

years.src: LTM: Minny Pops · Wikipedia: Minny Pops
years.h: Sparks in a Dark Room, FBN 15, recorded near Amsterdam
years.p: Self-produced late in 1981 at Arnold Mühren's studio: motorik pulses on 'Dream' and 'Trance', darker pieces like 'Black Eye'. NME loved it; Amsterdam's Vinyl magazine wasn't sure.
years.xp:
NME's Chris Bohn heard "tight, slight rhythm figures, out of which half melodies and exquisite synth lines spring." Vinyl's Dick Rijken found himself "at a bit of a loss confronted with the combination of disco and doom."

A July 1981 demo had already given up 'Een Kus', released as a flexi disc with Vinyl that October.

years.src: LTM: Minny Pops · Wikipedia: Minny Pops
years.h: 'Secret Story' is the second and last Factory single
years.p: Fac 57, backed with 'Island', follows the April Factory Benelux single 'Time' (FBN 11). The same month Wim Dekker and van Middendorp record their score for the play Poste Restante.

years.src: LTM: Minny Pops
years.h: A band meeting ends Minny Pops. Streetlife starts on Factory
years.p: The group breaks up after a meeting. Van Middendorp and Dekker carry on as Streetlife, making electro-dance 12-inches for Factory: 'Act On Instinct' (Fac 97) and 'No More Silence' (Fac 124).

years.src: LTM: Minny Pops · Electronic Sound
years.h: 4th Floor, one more album on Plurex
years.p: A reunion record two years after the split. Van Middendorp went on to executive jobs at Boudisque, PIAS, Sony and Roadrunner.

eras.title: Looser than they used to be
eras.text: Thirty years after their last gig, Minny Pops came back on Dutch radio, played the Melkweg again, and found themselves opening for Slash. Van Middendorp later moved the band to the UK and kept making records.

years.cap: Wally van Middendorp at the Melkweg, Amsterdam, April 7, 2012
years.src: LTM: Minny Pops · The Quietus · Wikipedia: Minny Pops
years.h: Back at the Melkweg, with Mark Ritsema on guitar
years.p: Announced on VPRO's 3voor12 in late 2011, the reunion's Dutch shows sell out after UK dates in Sheffield, Leeds, Manchester and London.
years.xp: "We used to be a very static band in the 80s, but now we've become much looser," van Middendorp told The Quietus. LTM also issued Standstill to Motion, a live set from the Melkweg on March 19, 1981, with a DVD of footage from 1979 to 1981.

years.src: LTM: Minny Pops
years.h: Minny Pops open for Slash at the Hammersmith Apollo
years.p: LTM's history calls it an unlikely support slot.

years.src: LTM: Minny Pops · Wikipedia: Minny Pops
years.h: Tim Burgess puts out the first new songs in decades
years.p: A double A-side 7-inch on [[Tim Burgess|f3a9f9c8-24e7-4465-9f2e-5ba02349e36c]]'s O Genesis label, recorded in Stockport.
years.xp: "I was pretty nervous about it," van Middendorp said. In the rehearsal room "things suddenly just clicked" and two new songs came out, which he called "a major departure from our early work."

years.src: Wikipedia: Minny Pops · Blowpipe
years.h: Stockholm 1974 takes its title from Patty Hearst's kidnapping
years.p: Made by a UK-based collective with players from Austin to Rotterdam, including Terry Edwards and Graham Dowdall. Blowpipe reissues it in 2024.
